name: Perkins Bass
bio: a Representative from New Hampshire; born in East Walpole, Norfolk County, Mass., October 6, 1912; graduated from Dartmouth College, Hanover, N.H., in 1934; graduated from Harvard Law School, Cambridge, Mass., in 1938; admitted to the New Hampshire bar in 1938; lawyer, private practice; law clerk to Judge Woodbury of First Circuit Court of Appeals in 1941 and 1942; United States Air Force, 1942-1945; served as air combat intelligence officer with General Chennault's Fourteenth Air Force in China from 1943 until discharged with rank of major in 1945; awarded the Bronze Star Medal and from the Nationalist Government of China received the Yun-Ma Medal for distinguished and meritorious service; resumed practice of law in Manchester and Peterborough, N.H.; member of the New Hampshire state house of representatives, 1939, 1941, 1947, and 1951; member of the New Hampshire state senate, 1949-1951, and as president; director and member of the executive committee of Bird & Son, Inc., East Walpole, Mass., 1948-1984; elected as a Republican to the Eighty-fourth and to the three succeeding Congresses (January 3, 1955-January 3, 1963); was not a candidate for renomination to the Eighty-eighth Congress in 1962, but was an unsuccessful candidate for the United States Senate; Republican National Committeeman from New Hampshire, 1964-1968; selectman of Peterborough, N.H., 1972-1976; died on October 25, 2011, in Peterborough, N.H.; interment at Pine Hill Cemetery, Peterborough, N.H.
